verdicts.title: The published LLM tutorial is built on distilgpt2, a model family the documentation elsewhere declares unsupported and whose gradient mismatch is still open (#813)
verdicts.reasoning: The load-bearing claim -- 'GPT-2 is not in any supported-family list' -- is false. GPT-2 is a first-class registered family: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/gpt2.py calls register_family('gpt2', ...) and `supported_families()` returns gpt2 (verified by running it: 26 families, gpt2 present). The user-facing support matrix, docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:165-180 ('Model compatibility ... The table shows vmap compatibility and which fused Triton kernels are applied per model'), contains the row `| GPT-2 | 124M, 355M | - | - | - | - | - | - |`, i.e. vmap-compatible with no Triton kernels. GPT-2 is also the model used in the two canonical quickstarts (docs/user-guide/huggingface/index.md:54 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/dptrainer.md:21-23 both call from_pretrained('gpt2')). The two sources the finding cites as authoritative are demonstrably non-exhaustive prose, not support matrices: README.md:161's feature bullet and the AGENTS.md 'Supported HF model families' section both also omit Mixtral, Qwen3-MoE, Qwen3.5-MoE, Qwen3-Next, HunYuan-V1-MoE, Mellum, GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4, all of which are registered families with rows in the same compatibility tables. So the tutorial targeting distilgpt2 is consistent with the documented support surface, and there is no docs-vs-support-matrix contradiction. What remains true is only that gpt2 sits in _GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES (packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:96-103) and that open issue #813 states gpt2 'genuinely fails vmap-grad parity' with a large mismatch on transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias; #813's acceptance criteria already require either fixing the gpt2 backward path or de-registering gpt2 from supported_families(), which would by itself force the tutorial change. The notebook-not-in-CI observation is correct (.github/workflows/pr.yml executes only accounting_and_calibration.ipynb, dp_sgd_training.ipynb, dp_ftrl_training.ipynb) but is a separate, generic coverage gap that applies equally to distributed_training.ipynb, privacy_auditing.ipynb, sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb and llm_finetuning.ipynb, and is not evidence of an unsupported model.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No defect established. GPT-2 is a registered, documented family (model-patches.md compatibility table, plus the gpt2 quickstarts), so the tutorial's use of distilgpt2 does not misrepresent the support surface. The only real residual is open issue #813: gpt2's vmap(grad) gradients do not match upstream and the parity exemption is a plain skip; if #813 is resolved by de-registering gpt2 rather than fixing it, docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb and the two gpt2 quickstarts must all be retargeted at the same time.

verdicts.title: Distributed reference names `opaque.distributed._state.register_sync_type`, a module path that does not exist
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree. docs/reference/distributed.md:80-86 reads: 'The sync() machinery is type-dispatched: clipping and noise states register themselves with `opaque.distributed._state.register_sync_type` and provide the right per-state aggregation rule. Lower-level scalar reductions, tensor gathers, and object syncs live in `_state.py`'. Ran `uv run python -c "import opaque.distributed as d; print(hasattr(d,'register_sync_type')); import importlib; importlib.import_module('opaque.distributed._state')"` -> prints `False` then `ModuleNotFoundError No module named 'opaque.distributed._state'`. The facade packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/distributed/__init__.py re-exports only 16 names (all_reduce, barrier, gather_for_metrics, get_rank, get_world_size, is_distributed, is_main_process, local_shard, num_processes, process_index, reduce_pytree, reduce_pytree_, sum_gradients, sum_gradients_, sync, wait_for_everyone) -- no register_sync_type, and the package directory holds only collectives.py, gradients.py, __init__.py, py.typed. The real symbol is at packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/distributed/_state.py:537 and is re-exported from opaque.api.engine.distributed (__init__.py:22); every registrant imports it from there (opaque-dpftrl/.../noise/_distributed.py:20, opaque-optimizers/.../distributed.py:42, opaque-engine/.../clipping/_distributed.py:21, .../profiling/_distributed.py:15). mkdocs --strict cannot catch it because the bad path is inline prose in backticks, not a `:::` mkdocstrings directive (the neighbouring `::: opaque.distributed.gradients.*` directives do resolve). One extra instance of the same wrong path exists in a source docstring: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_distributed.py:6 says 'self-registers via :func:`opaque.distributed.register_sync_type`', which would also fail to resolve as a Sphinx/mkdocstrings cross-reference. Impact is contributor-facing only: one ImportError while extending the sync registry. No user-facing API, no privacy effect. Not a duplicate of any open tracked issue (#775/#845 cover citation verification, not API paths).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A contributor adding a new sync-able DP state follows docs/reference/distributed.md:82 and writes `from opaque.distributed._state import register_sync_type`, which raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.distributed._state' (the facade exports no register_sync_type at all). The working import is `from opaque.api.engine.distributed import register_sync_type` (or `...distributed._state`). Documentation-only; nothing at runtime or in accounting is affected.

verdicts.title: Two user-guide pages point 'runnable reference' readers at test files that do not exist at the given paths
verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly. docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:172 'Runnable references' lists '`tests/integration/test_dpsgd_pipeline.py` - minimal smoke test exercising the same flow on a tiny LlamaConfig + LoRA model (and the Qwen2 variant for the real-HF case)', and docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md:249 has the identical shape for test_dpftrl_pipeline.py. `ls tests/integration/` shows only README.md, __pycache__, accounting, alignment, conftest.py, ddp, noise, rng, sampling, transformers -- no test_*.py at that level. `find . -name test_dpsgd_pipeline.py -o -name test_dpftrl_pipeline.py` returns ./tests/integration/transformers/test_dpsgd_pipeline.py and ./tests/integration/transformers/test_dpftrl_pipeline.py, i.e. the files live one directory deeper. The target files are the ones the prose describes (test_dpsgd_pipeline.py's module docstring: 'A tiny synthetic LlamaConfig (fast - runs in the PR gate)' and 'Real Qwen2-0.5B from HuggingFace Hub (marked slow)'), so only the path segment `transformers/` is missing in both links. Trivial docs drift, reader-visible but recoverable in seconds; no runtime, API or privacy consequence. I did not re-verify the finding's side claim about what OPQ-370 / sweep #844 covered -- irrelevant to whether the two paths resolve today, which they do not.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader of the DP-SGD or DP-FTRL guide runs `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_dpsgd_pipeline.py` (or test_dpftrl_pipeline.py) and pytest exits with 'file or directory not found'. The correct paths are tests/integration/transformers/test_dpsgd_pipeline.py and tests/integration/transformers/test_dpftrl_pipeline.py; the files themselves exist and match the prose description.

verdicts.title: Patching gpt_oss / deepseek_v4 silently deletes the attention sink and freezes the `sinks` parameter
verdicts.reasoning: Independently reproduced on transformers 5.15.1. Chain verified link by link: (1) make_apply_family_patches defaults eager_attention_replacement=vmap_eager_attention_forward (packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_family.py:126) and rebinds mod.eager_attention_forward when the `eager_attention` concern is on (_family.py:212-216); (2) that concern defaults from `compat`, which defaults True (_factory.py:241-247 doc + apply() signature), so it needs no opt-in; (3) models/gpt_oss.py:16-19 passes no override, models/deepseek_v4.py:16-20 overrides only rope_replacement=None; (4) vmap_eager_attention_forward (components/attention.py:365-387) ends in **kwargs and delegates to _grouped_eager_attention, a plain softmax with no sink term -- `grep -rn 'sinks\|s_aux' packages/opaque-patches/src/` returns zero hits; (5) upstream GptOssAttention.forward passes `s_aux=self.sinks` into the resolved attention interface and its eager_attention_forward concatenates the sink logit before the softmax (inspected the installed source); DeepseekV4 eager_attention_forward likewise contains sinks; both families have _supports_sdpa=False, so eager is the only non-flash path. (6) Reproduction with DEFAULT kwargs: tiny GptOssForCausalLM, config._attn_implementation resolves to 'eager'; after apply_model_patches(m2) the module global is vmap_eager_attention_forward, max abs logit diff vs the unpatched model is 1.545e-01, and after a backward pass model.layers[0].self_attn.sinks.grad is None. Same script for a tiny DeepseekV4ForCausalLM: max abs logit diff 1.065e-01, model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks.grad is None. No warning is emitted, and `grep -rn -i sink docs/` returns nothing. The doc contradiction is real: docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218 says that for GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4 'only RMSNorm, RoPE (where standard), and cross-entropy are patched'. Two corrections to the finding. (a) Already tracked: open issue #813 ('Convert parity skips to strict xfail and resolve the gpt2 gradient mismatch', parent #769) explicitly scopes 'The remaining three exemptions are each justified in the reason string or removed', and its open closing PR #1032 names this exact defect verbatim -- the new xfail reason for both families is 'the required eager-attention compatibility shim omits the upstream self-attention sink gradient'. So the sink gap is known and in flight; the only genuinely new delta is the model-patches.md:215-218 claim and the absence of any user-facing warning. (b) The first fix option is wrong: passing eager_attention_replacement=None (the gpt2 treatment) would leave upstream's hardcoded 4-D eager attention in place (reshape(1,-1,1,1).expand(query.shape[0],...), transpose(1,2)), which is exactly what breaks under vmap -- hence 'the required ... compatibility shim'. Only the sink-aware vmap shim (forwarding s_aux into the softmax) is a real fix. Severity lowered from high to medium: no privacy effect (clipping still bounds per-record sensitivity and accounting is untouched), it is confined to two opt-in model families, the gap is acknowledged in-repo in the parity skip comments and in the in-flight PR, and the trained model is degraded rather than silently wrong in an unbounded way -- but it is silent at defaults and contradicted by the docs table, which keeps it above low.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Fine-tuning a GPT-OSS or DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint through DPTrainer or any apply_model_patches(model) flow with DEFAULT kwargs (compat=True -> eager_attention on) rebinds transformers.models.{gpt_oss,deepseek_v4}.modeling_*.eager_attention_forward to opaque's vmap_eager_attention_forward, which swallows the s_aux kwarg and omits the attention-sink logit from the softmax. Reproduced on transformers 5.15.1 with tiny configs: forward logits shift by 1.54e-01 (gpt_oss) / 1.07e-01 (deepseek_v4) max abs versus the unpatched model, and after a backward pass model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks.grad is None, so the sink parameter never trains. No warning is emitted. Both families are exempted from forward parity (_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES) and gradient parity (_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES) in packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:87-103, so CI cannot flag it. Privacy accounting is unaffected; the defect is model fidelity, and it is contradicted by docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218. The sink-gradient half is already named in open issue #813 and its closing PR #1032; the doc claim and the missing warning are not.
